definitions.explanation: The number one when counting things using native Japanese numbers.

examples.japanese: りんごを{一|ひと}つください。
{一|ひと}つだけ{残|のこ}っています。
{一|ひと}つ{質問|しつもん}があります。
{子供|こども}は{一|ひと}つです。
examples.english: The child is one year old.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つも{残|のこ}っていない。
{娘|むすめ}が{一|ひと}つになった。
{一|ひと}つずつ{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: I'll check them one by one.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つ{上|うえ}の{学年|がくねん}だ。
まだ{一|ひと}つなのに{話|はな}せる。
examples.english: They can talk even though they're only one.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つお{願|ねが}いがあります。
examples.english: I have one favor to ask.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{一|ひと}つになったので、お{祝|いわ}いをした。
examples.english: The baby turned one, so we had a celebration.

examples.japanese: うちの{子|こ}は{一|ひと}つの{時|とき}に{初|はじ}めて{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: Our child took their first steps at age one.

notes:
{一|ひと}つ is the native Japanese number 'one,' used for counting general items and as part of many set expressions.

NATIVE COUNTING (1-10):
- {一|ひと}つ, {二|ふた}つ, {三|みっ}つ, {四|よっ}つ, {五|いつ}つ
- {六|むっ}つ, {七|なな}つ, {八|やっ}つ, {九|ここの}つ, {十|とお}

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一|ひと}つずつ: one by one
- {一|ひと}つも + negative: not even one
- {一|ひと}つ{上|うえ}: one level/year above
- {一|ひと}つお{願|ねが}い: one request/favor

AGE:
Used informally for age one: {子供|こども}が{一|ひと}つになった (the child turned one). This native system (ひとつ, ふたつ...) is used for young children's ages up to about nine.

USAGE:
This native counting system is used for general items when no specific counter applies, or when the counter is unknown.
